patent_grounding.rationale: The hub, rigid material, axial bore, substantially circumferential flexibility-providing slit, drive shaft received at one end, driven shaft attached at the other, transmission of rotational force, and convex/receding outer-end geometry are supported by passage 986d7d07954ac3bd7ccbe206f2808be0. The external shaft context is also reflected in claim text in b7f6116e21588cac4a0d2801ab5b585f. No invented numerical constraints, controls, or material specification appear.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model captures rotational-force transmission and hub flexibility, with the core patent structure. It omits optional dependent-claim inner-periphery geometry and unspecified controls/limits rather than guessing.

flow_consistency.rationale: Revision 2 declares mechanically rotational compatible ports, and DRIVE_SHAFT.DRIVE_TORQUE_OUT connects to HUB.HUB_TORQUE_IN via DRIVE_TORQUE; HUB.HUB_TORQUE_OUT connects to DRIVEN_SHAFT.DRIVEN_TORQUE_IN via OUTPUT_TORQUE. Direction and stated roles form the intended drive→hub→driven path.

claim_traceability.rationale: The transmit and flexibility functions and hub geometry correspond to claim language in 986d7d07954ac3bd7ccbe206f2808be0; shaft arrangement is directly supported in 986d7d07954ac3bd7ccbe206f2808be0 and b7f6116e21588cac4a0d2801ab5b585f. No unsupported requirements are added.

interfaces.rationale: The two explicit interfaces mate existing subsystem IDs and compatible port IDs, each references an existing flow, and each connection is recorded once (on the source/owning subsystem). Shaft placement and force transmission are patent-grounded.

textbook_application.rationale: The model distinguishes physical components from verb-noun functions and separates context shafts from the coupling hub; directed interfaces/flows give an intelligible boundary path. This is consistent with retrieved guidance on functional decomposition and context flows without treating textbook content as invention evidence.

summary: Independent review of saved SJS revision 2: previous disconnected-path concern is resolved. The drive-shaft output→hub input and hub output→driven-shaft input interfaces reference the corresponding flows with compatible mechanical_rotational port types and appropriate directions. The represented hub, function, and shaft relationships are grounded in the cited patent passages; no structural findings are reported. No unresolved review findings identified.
